extracted.subtask_description: Practical standards and procedures for mercantile accounting: how to keep inventory (inventario), journal (giornale), memoriale and quaderno; how to record, value, transfer, reconcile, and authenticate commercial entries and compute gains/losses and partner shares.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain an up-to-date inventory (inventario)
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep a full inventario listing all goods, movable and immovable property, credits, and other principal items necessary for the merchant business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The inventario is the principal register: list each item by name, quantity and valuation; include precious metals, jewels, fabrics, ships and cargo, and other assets. Produce a complete exemplar with formalities (’esemplare con tutte sue solennià’). Use the inventario to derive the merchant’s true capital and to aid in bookkeeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep a quaderno, giornale and memoriale with distinct roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Use separate books: a quaderno (notebook), giornale (daybook/journal), and memoriale; each has a defined purpose in the accounting system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The quaderno should hold running notes and ledgers useful for daily reference; the giornale records day-to-day transactions; the memoriale gathers particulars and supporting documents. Keep them organized so any transaction can be found according to chapter/number. Cross-reference entries among these books when preparing balances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare and record a clear alfabeto/conteggio (index and numbering)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an alphabetical index and page/account numbering to facilitate lookup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The quaderno should have an 'alfabeto conto' and pages properly numbered; order parties alphabetically and number entries so that the reader can find related documents and entries by chapter or number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record both Dare e Avere (debit and credit) explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: Every entry should show debit and credit amounts, with proper notation of the two numbers (the two 'numeri' or carti).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place debit and credit figures in the prescribed columns/margins, and ensure the two numbers for each partita are recorded for reconciliation; use the same conventions across books to avoid confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document all supporting papers and correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep copies of letters, receipts, public documents and other papers associated with transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register letters and important documents in a letters register (registro delle lettere) and attach or reference them in the quaderno/giornale; these documents serve as proof for claims and are to be preserved with the books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticate and legalize principal books
rubrics_metrics.description: Have books authenticated where required, and keep principal merchant books in a form acceptable for official or legal review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many entries note that principal books should be 'autetificare' and maintained formally; follow local practices for notarization or official registration to strengthen evidentiary value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep special ledgers for petty or recurring small items
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep separate particular books (libri particolari) for petty entries, small trades, or recurring minor items rather than clogging main books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create small private ledgers for small merchandise, trips, or petty matters so the main journal/inventario remains clear; these particular books may be referenced back to the giornale/quaderno when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record barter, companies and partnership particulars distinctly
rubrics_metrics.description: When goods are exchanged by baratto or transactions involve companies (compagnie), record the nature of the barter, partners’ shares and terms explicitly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document the items exchanged, the agreed valuation, each partner’s contribution and share of profits/losses; enter these as specific partite in the books and keep a clear account of capital and advantages assigned to each party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuate goods consistently, taking quality into account
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining value (e.g., cloth, panni), adjust price according to quality, dye, weight, and other attributes rather than treating all units equally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show cloth valuations depending on color, fineness and defects; use proportional calculations (scaling by quality) and, for complex cases, consult or prepare a table (tabula) to compute aggregate values and conversions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use tables (tabula) or systematic methods for repetitive computations
rubrics_metrics.description: For recurring, complex arithmetic (e.g., converting many lots or computing shares), prepare tables to simplify calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text advises using tabula to handle numerous multiplications and conversions (e.g., many small cloth lots) to avoid mistakes; the table becomes a universal aid for repetitive computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconcile books annually and perform a formal bilancio (balance)
rubrics_metrics.description: At regular intervals (commonly annually) close out books, carry balances, and prepare a formal bilancio reconciling giornale, memoriale and inventario.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not write in old books when closing — transfer totals to a new book; record the method to carry one book into another and document reasons for discrepancies. The bilancio should show the final state of capital and be supported by the books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report and transfer entries between books with transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: When moving entries from one book to another (e.g., old quaderno to new), report them clearly and keep cross‑references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the page/number references (reportare un libro in l’altro), note the transferred totals and keep the proper chronological/orderly transfer so entries can be traced back to originals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct errors by formal retraction and reallocation
rubrics_metrics.description: If entries are erroneous, retract them or move them to the correct place with a clear record, avoiding clandestine alterations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual prescribes manner and order to 'retractare' or 'ritornarc' partite moved by error: indicate the correction, where it was moved, and the reason; preserve audit trail rather than erasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep accounts with public offices and record official transactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a record of dealings with public authorities (camera, customs, etc.) and include their entries in the books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text notes the method for keeping account with public offices and the importance of these records for mercantile administration; include taxes, duties, and official charges as distinct entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record journeys and travellers’ accounts separately
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep specific partite for voyages, travelers’ expenses and aggregates connected to journeys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create one or more notebooks for travel accounts (conti dei viaggi) so that travel-related income and expenses are clearly separable and can be consolidated by trip.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish capital vs revenue and compute gains/losses on resale
rubrics_metrics.description: Track capital invested, returns, and gains/losses from buying and re-selling merchandise; compute how much capital and profit each operation produces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples walk through cloth purchases/resales, showing how to compute resulting capital and profit per lot and aggregate. Use the inventario and bilancio to show how capital changes over time and how to allocate gains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record partner advantages and apportion benefits mathematically
rubrics_metrics.description: When partners receive advantages (e.g., extra capital, profit share), quantify and record the amounts and apportion them according to agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual demonstrates computing proportionate advantages and recalculating capital shares; document the computation and enter the apportioned amounts in the partners’ accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not write new matters in closed/older books when preparing balances
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid adding new entries into books that are being used for balance or historical recordkeeping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain integrity of closed books by transferring totals rather than altering original pages; this preserves the evidentiary and archival value of earlier records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clear headings and chapter/partite ordering for entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize entries into chapters/partite and maintain consistent order so that related items appear together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use chapter numbers and consistent ordering across the quaderno and giornale; this helps readers find where particular goods or transactions are recorded and eases compilation of summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep a named list of principal goods and their particulars (descriptive catalogue)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each significant item in the inventario, record descriptive particulars (e.g., type of cloth, silverware, jewels) and, where appropriate, marks or unique identifiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List movable and immovable goods, their distinguishing features, weights, and known markings so they can be identified and valued if needed. This also helps with customs and legal claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record the method and date of valuation changes and mutations
rubrics_metrics.description: When the value of goods or capital is re-expressed (mutated), record the date, method and reason for the change in the books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark the mutation at the head of the relevant page and give reasons so future readers understand why valuations differ; this is useful at balance time and for dispute resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain brevity and clarity in entries to aid future use
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries should be concise and clear, omitting extraneous commentary so the book serves as a practical working document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The epilogue emphasizes brief, orderly accounts that enable others to understand the business and its credit; a reader should be able to take up the books and discern the merchant’s obligations and credits without undue confusion.
